title: Consumer confidence weakened while the aggregate price level rose and unemployment stayed comparatively low
source_unit: Monthly US aggregate FRED series: University of Michigan consumer sentiment, CPI for all urban consumers, and civilian unemployment rate

observations.method: FRED graph CSV extraction of UMCSENT, CPIAUCSL, and UNRATE at monthly frequency; January 2024 is the comparison baseline.
observations.uncertainty: FRED republishes source series and revisions; the three series have different constructions and populations. Aggregate indexes do not measure a common household, lived inflation, purchasing power, or political response.
observations.subgroup: US aggregate; no household, income, age, race, geography, or political subgroup.
observations.counterinterpretation: Sentiment may reflect expectations, politics, financial markets, or events in addition to current prices and employment. A baseline point cannot identify the cause of later movement.

observations.method: Monthly FRED levels with changes calculated against the January 2024 observation from the same downloaded series.
observations.uncertainty: The changes are descriptive co-movement, not a causal estimate. CPI is an aggregate price index and sentiment is a survey index; neither supplies the household-specific basket or financial buffer.
observations.counterinterpretation: A modest index-level price increase can feel very different across households, and sentiment can move for reasons unrelated to the measured CPI level.

observations.method: Monthly FRED levels with changes calculated against January 2024.
observations.uncertainty: The series do not share a respondent or household denominator. The unemployment rate is a labor-market aggregate, not a measure of job quality, hours, income adequacy, or household room.
observations.counterinterpretation: The sentiment decline may incorporate expected future conditions, political interpretation, or other shocks; its timing alone does not identify price causation.

observations.method: Monthly FRED levels with changes calculated against January 2024; July 2026 is the latest month with a non-missing UMCSENT value in the retrieved file.
observations.uncertainty: Later observations are subject to revision and the August 2026 sentiment value was missing in the retrieved file. No causal, household-level, or political-behavior inference is made.
observations.counterinterpretation: Sentiment partially recovered from December 2025 while remaining below January 2024; that recovery cautions against treating the series as a one-way response to prices.

related_sources.claim: Federal Reserve SHED provides household-level economic well-being and adaptation measures that aggregate sentiment cannot supply.
BEA national accounts provide income, spending, and price-flow context at a different aggregation level.

boundary: This is a descriptive FRED aggregate time-series layer. It supports a timing comparison among consumer sentiment, the aggregate price index, and unemployment; it does not establish inflation causation, household hardship, purchasing power, consumer choice, political attribution, or trust. The FRED CSV was downloaded for this pass but the raw file is not committed; the query URL and retrieval hash preserve the captured input identity.
